caught_by: a paragraph with no bold lead is a caveat too: untriaged: wanted 1, got 0
a bold-lead caveat and a plain one are both found, and counted once: untriaged: wanted 2, got 1
a bold caveat keeps its key when plain paragraphs are read too: untriaged: wanted 1, got 0

cases.name: the key becomes the whole paragraph, orphaning every bold verdict
cases.old: claim = lead.group(1) if lead else stripped
caught_by: a verdict is read by the opening of its bullet: open: wanted 1, got 0; untriaged: wanted 1, got 2; problems: wanted 0, got 1 ['a.md::It does not do the first thing.']
closed without naming what closed it is refused: closed: wanted 1, got 0
deliberate without naming the reasoning is refused: deliberate: wanted 1, got 0
narrowed without naming what closed and what is left is refused: narrowed: wanted 1, got 0; problems: wanted 2, got 1 ['a.md::It does not do the first thing.']
narrowed with a `by` and no `residual` is refused: narrowed: wanted 1, got 0
narrowed with a `by` and a `residual` is accepted and counted as its own thing: narrowed: wanted 1, got 0; problems: wanted 0, got 1 ['a.md::It does not do the first thing.']
a settled verdict carrying `checked` rather than `reviewed` is refused: deliberate: wanted 1, got 0
a narrowed caveat carrying `reviewed` rather than `checked` is refused: narrowed: wanted 1, got 0
